definition_zh: v. 解毒；去除毒素；帮助戒除（酒瘾或毒瘾）
definition_en: to remove poisonous substances from a body or thing, or to help a person stop taking drugs or alcohol
core_image: 肝脏把一杯酒里的酒精分解成无害的水和二氧化碳；戒断中心里，一个人床头的酒瓶被换成水杯
scene: 肝脏能分解酒精。The liver detoxifies alcohol.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：detoxifies 指解毒、分解毒素；句意是肝脏能分解酒精。

senses.title: Remove poison from a body
senses.definition: to remove poisonous substances from a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 从人或动物体内去除有毒物质
senses.example: The liver detoxifies alcohol.
senses.exampleCN: 肝脏能分解酒精。
senses.why: A filter turning dark water clear.
senses.whyCN: 一个把黑水变清的过滤器。

senses.title: Break down a toxin
senses.definition: to change a harmful substance into a harmless one
senses.definitionCN: 把有害物质变成无害物质
senses.example: Enzymes detoxify the drug in the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 酶把血液中的药物分解掉。
senses.why: A molecule split into two harmless parts.
senses.whyCN: 一个被拆成两个无害部分的分子。

senses.title: Help someone stop a habit
senses.definition: to help a person stop taking drugs or drinking alcohol
senses.definitionCN: 帮助一个人停止吸毒或饮酒
senses.example: The clinic detoxifies patients over two weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所在两周内帮病人完成戒断。
senses.why: A water glass on a bedside table where a bottle stood.
senses.whyCN: 床头柜上一只水杯，原先那里放着酒瓶。

intro.en: Detoxify is de- away plus toxic, from Greek toxikon, arrow poison, from toxon, a bow, plus -ify, to make.
intro.cn: detoxify 由 de-（去掉）加 toxic（有毒的）加 -ify（使成为）构成；toxic 来自希腊语 toxikon（箭毒），toxikon 又来自 toxon（弓）。

items.en: Toxon meant a bow.
items.cn: 希腊语 toxon 意为弓。

items.en: Toxikon meant poison for arrows.
items.cn: toxikon 意为涂在箭上的毒。

items.en: Toxicum carried the poison sense into Latin.
items.cn: 拉丁语 toxicum 承接了毒的意思。

items.en: Toxic entered English for poisonous.
items.cn: 十七世纪 toxic 以有毒义进入英语。

items.en: Detoxify was formed for removing poison.
items.cn: 二十世纪 detoxify 被造出来表示去毒。

items.en: Detox now also names a short diet.
items.cn: 如今 detox 也指短期排毒饮食。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tox- poison family; the near-meaning group names other ways of making something safe.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tox-（毒）家族；近义组是其他表示「使变安全」的词。

entries.definition: Poisonous; it is the middle part of detoxify.
entries.definitionCN: 有毒的；它是 detoxify 的中间部分。

entries.definition: A poisonous substance made by a living thing.
entries.definitionCN: 生物体产生的有毒物质。

entries.definition: The state of being drunk; it adds in- to the same poison root.
entries.definitionCN: 醉酒状态；在同一毒词根上加 in-。

entries.definition: To remove dirty or harmful parts from something.
entries.definitionCN: 去掉某物中脏污或有害的部分。

entries.definition: To make something thoroughly clean.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物彻底干净。

entries.definition: To stop something having an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物不再起作用。

normalIntro.en: Detoxify is de- away plus tox- poison plus -ify make: make the poison go away.
normalIntro.cn: detoxify 就是 de-（去掉）加 tox-（毒）加 -ify（使）：让毒消失。

normal.en: Tox- means poison, from arrow poison.
normal.cn: tox- 意为毒，来自箭毒。

normal.en: -ify means to make.
normal.cn: -ify 表示使成为。

normal.en: Detox is the short everyday form.
normal.cn: detox 是日常的简短说法。

normal.en: Detoxify takes from for a habit.
normal.cn: detoxify 表戒断时后接 from。

normal.en: The liver detoxifies alcohol every day.
normal.cn: 肝脏每天都在分解酒精。

abstract.en: A filter turning dark water clear.
abstract.cn: 一个把黑水变清的过滤器。

abstract.en: A molecule split into two harmless parts.
abstract.cn: 一个被拆成两个无害部分的分子。

abstract.en: A water glass on a bedside table where a bottle stood.
abstract.cn: 床头柜上一只水杯，原先那里放着酒瓶。

examples.en: The body detoxifies waste through the kidneys.
examples.cn: 身体通过肾脏排出废物毒素。

examples.en: She detoxified at a clinic last spring.
examples.cn: 她去年春天在诊所完成了戒断。

examples.en: These plants help detoxify the soil.
examples.cn: 这些植物有助于净化土壤。

dict_mnemonic.text: detoxify ＝ de（去掉）＋ tox（毒，希腊语 toxon「弓」→ toxikon「箭毒」）＋ -ify（使）＝使毒去掉，「解毒」。

root: 希腊语 toxon（弓）→ toxikon（箭毒）→ 拉丁语 toxicum → toxic（有毒的）→ de-＋toxic＋-ify → detoxify

sensesIntro.en: One poison made harmless: a filter, a split molecule and a water glass.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种被变无害的毒：一个过滤器、一个被拆开的分子与一只水杯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a filter turning dark water clear as the poison is held back
core.cn: 核心意象：一个过滤器把黑水变清，毒物被拦下来

branches.en: A filter turning dark water clear.
branches.cn: 一个把黑水变清的过滤器。

branches.en: A molecule split into two harmless parts.
branches.cn: 一个被拆成两个无害部分的分子。

branches.en: A water glass on a bedside table where a bottle stood.
branches.cn: 床头柜上一只水杯，原先那里放着酒瓶。

branches.en: Both turn something harmful into something safe.
branches.cn: 两者都把有害的东西变成安全的。

branches.en: Both happen inside a living body.
branches.cn: 两者都发生在活的身体里。

intro.en: Detoxify is de- plus tox- plus -ify; the poison root also builds toxin and toxicology.
intro.cn: detoxify 由 de- 加 tox- 加 -ify 构成；毒这个词根也造出 toxin 与 toxicology。

latinIntro.en: Latin toxicum means poison, facere to make and purus clean.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 toxicum 意为毒，facere 意为做，purus 意为干净。

definition_zh: 减损；贬低；有损于；分散（注意）
definition_en: to reduce the value, quality or reputation of something
core_image: 一面完好的墙上被划出一道浅痕，整面墙看上去都不再完整
scene: 那道裂缝本来很小，但每次有人经过都会先看它一眼。A few scratches detract from the beauty of the table.
sceneCN: 这里 detract 指使某物的美感减损（第 1 个义项：减损价值）；句意为几道划痕有损这张桌子的美感。

senses.title: Reduce value or quality
senses.definition: to make something less valuable or less good
senses.definitionCN: 使某物价值降低或品质变差
senses.example: A few scratches detract from the beauty of the table.
senses.exampleCN: 几道划痕有损这张桌子的美感。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to draw away'; value is drawn off the way water is drawn from a full vessel.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「拉走」；价值被拉走，就像水从满的容器里被舀出。

senses.title: Diminish an achievement
senses.definition: to make an accomplishment seem smaller than it is
senses.definitionCN: 使一项成就显得比实际更小
senses.example: Nothing can detract from what the team achieved.
senses.exampleCN: 没有什么能贬低这个团队所取得的成就。
senses.why: Praise adds weight, and detraction removes it; the same scale is used in both directions.
senses.whyCN: 赞扬增加分量，贬低则移除分量；两个方向用的是同一杆秤。

senses.title: Spoil a pleasing quality
senses.definition: to lessen the pleasure or attractiveness of something
senses.definitionCN: 减少某物的愉悦感或吸引力
senses.example: The noisy road detracts from the charm of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 嘈杂的道路有损这座房子的魅力。
senses.why: Charm is a delicate balance; one wrong element pulls the whole composition down.
senses.whyCN: 魅力是一种精细的平衡；一个不对的元素就把整个构图拉低。

senses.title: Divert attention
senses.definition: to draw attention away from the main matter
senses.definitionCN: 把注意力从主要事情上引开
senses.example: Constant notifications detract attention from the work.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的通知分散了对工作的注意。
senses.why: Attention is a finite beam; whatever detracts turns part of it elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 注意力是一束有限的光；任何减损都把其中一部分转向别处。

senses.title: Speak disparagingly
senses.definition: to speak of someone in a way that lowers their standing
senses.definitionCN: 以降低他人地位的方式谈论某人
senses.example: He never missed a chance to detract from his rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 他从不放过贬低对手的机会。
senses.why: Words can remove value from a reputation as surely as scratches remove it from a table.
senses.whyCN: 言语能从名声上拿走价值，正如划痕能从桌子上拿走价值。

senses.title: Harm a reputation
senses.definition: to damage the good name of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 损害个人或团体的好名声
senses.example: The scandal detracted from the university's reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻损害了这所大学的声誉。
senses.why: Reputation is held by others, so it can be lowered by talk even when nothing has changed.
senses.whyCN: 声誉由他人持有，因此即使事实未变，也能被言论拉低。

senses.title: Lessen enjoyment
senses.definition: to reduce the pleasure of an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 减少某个场合的乐趣
senses.example: One rude guest detracted from the whole evening.
senses.exampleCN: 一个无礼的客人破坏了整个夜晚。
senses.why: Pleasure is a total made of many small contributions, and one rude guest removes more than their own share.
senses.whyCN: 愉悦由许多小的贡献构成一个总数，而一个无礼的客人拿走的比他自己那一份更多。

senses.title: Subtract, in old use
senses.definition: in older mathematics, to take away a quantity
senses.definitionCN: 在旧时数学中，减去一个量
senses.example: The old text says to detract three from ten.
senses.exampleCN: 旧文本说从十中减去三。
senses.why: The arithmetic sense is the literal skeleton: detraction is subtraction applied to value.
senses.whyCN: 算术义是字面的骨架：减损就是把减法用在价值上。

intro.en: Detract comes from a Latin verb meaning to draw away, and the image of subtraction runs through every sense.
intro.cn: detract 来自一个意为「拉走」的拉丁动词，「减法」的意象贯穿所有义项。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the 15c. and fixed the phrase detract from for value and reputation.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个动词，并用 detract from 固定搭配表示价值与声誉的减损。

items.en: Detrahere meant 'to draw off, take away', from de- 'away' and trahere 'to draw'.
items.cn: detrahere 意为「拉走、拿走」，由 de-「离开」与 trahere「拉」构成。

items.en: Trahere 'to draw' also gives traction, tractor and attract, all about pulling.
items.cn: trahere「拉」也产生 traction、tractor 与 attract，都与拖拉有关。

items.en: Detractio meant 'a taking away', used for both subtraction and slander.
items.cn: detractio 意为「拿走」，既用于减法，也用于诽谤。

items.en: The word moved from arithmetic to reputation: to detract from a person is to subtract from their standing.
items.cn: 这个词从算术移到声誉：贬低一个人，就是从其地位中减去。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tract root; the near-meaning group names kinds of reduction.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tract 词根；近义组列出各种削减。

entries.definition: the act of belittling or reducing value.
entries.definitionCN: 贬低或减损价值的行为。

entries.definition: someone who criticizes and lessens another's worth.
entries.definitionCN: 批评并贬低他人价值的人。

entries.definition: To draw together or become smaller; it shares tract- but pulls in rather than taking away.
entries.definitionCN: 拉拢或缩小；共享 tract-，但是往里拉而非拿走。

entries.definition: to draw something toward oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物拉向自己。

entries.definition: to make something seem or become smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物显得或变得更小。

entries.definition: to weaken something gradually and indirectly.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐间接地削弱某物。

entries.definition: to speak of someone or something as unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人或某物说得不重要。

entries.definition: To reduce the value or worth of something.
entries.definitionCN: 降低某物的价值。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of a scratch on an otherwise perfect surface.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想把「完好表面上的一道划痕」这一画面留住。

normal.en: Tract means to draw; detract means to draw value away.
normal.cn: tract 意为拉；detract 就是把价值拉走。

normal.en: Think of a subtraction sign in front of a reputation.
normal.cn: 想象在声誉前面放一个减号。

normal.en: Picture a fine table with one deep scratch; the eye keeps returning to it.
normal.cn: 想象一张好桌子上有一道深划痕；目光总回到那里。

normal.en: Say dih-TRAKT, one clean pull away from the whole.
normal.cn: 读成 dih-TRAKT，从整体上干净地拉走一次。

normal.en: Link it with diminish: both make the total smaller.
normal.cn: 把它和 diminish 联系：两者都让总量变小。

abstract.en: Value can be removed without anything being taken.
abstract.cn: 不必拿走任何东西，价值也能被移除。

abstract.en: A single wrong element can pull down a whole composition.
abstract.cn: 一个不对的元素就能拉低整个构图。

abstract.en: Slander is subtraction performed on a person's standing.
abstract.cn: 诽谤就是在人的地位上做减法。

examples.en: A few scratches detract from the beauty of the table.
examples.cn: 几道划痕有损这张桌子的美感。

examples.en: The noisy road detracts from the charm of the house.
examples.cn: 嘈杂的道路有损这座房子的魅力。

examples.en: The scandal detracted from the university's reputation.
examples.cn: 丑闻损害了这所大学的声誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: de（离开）+ tract（拉）：把价值或注意力拉走，就是「减损」。

root: 拉丁语 detrahere（拉走）：de-（离开）+ trahere（拉）

sensesIntro.en: Detract always takes something away from a whole; the senses differ in whether what is removed is value, standing, pleasure or attention.
sensesIntro.cn: detract 始终从整体上拿走一点东西；各义项的差别在于被拿走的是价值、地位、乐趣还是注意力。

core.en: VALUE IS DRAWN AWAY
core.cn: 价值被拉走

branches.en: Beauty and quality reduced by a small flaw.
branches.cn: 被小瑕疵削减的美感与品质。

branches.en: Achievements and rivals measured downward by talk.
branches.cn: 被言论压低的分量与对手。

branches.en: Attention pulled away from the main matter.
branches.cn: 从主要事情上被拉走的注意力。

branches.en: Reputations and occasions that lose their shine.
branches.cn: 失去光彩的声誉与场合。

branches.en: The old arithmetic sense of subtracting.
branches.cn: 减去的古老算术义。

intro.en: The word belongs to the tract family, where every member involves pulling.
intro.cn: 这个词属于 tract 词族，其中每个成员都涉及「拉」。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere 'to draw' supplies a large family of English words about pulling and dragging.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere「拉」提供了大量关于拖拉的英语词。

items.meaning: the act of taking value away
items.example: The article was a long detraction of his career.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章是对他职业生涯的长篇贬损。

items.example: His detractors called the plan naive.
items.exampleCN: 贬低他的人称这个计划天真。

items.example: The fence is detracting from the view.
The remarks were detractive rather than helpful.
items.exampleCN: 这些话是贬损性的，而非有帮助的。

items.example: The exhibit attracts thousands of visitors.
items.exampleCN: 这个展览吸引成千上万的参观者。

items.example: The tires lost traction on the ice.
items.exampleCN: 轮胎在冰上失去了抓地力。

items.example: The tractor pulled the broken cart.
items.exampleCN: 拖拉机拉走了坏掉的车。

items.example: The idea is too abstract to picture.
items.exampleCN: 这个观念太抽象，难以想象。

definition_zh: adj. 有害的；损害的；造成伤害的
definition_en: causing harm or loss to health, interests or a system
core_image: 一张桌子上，酸液滴落留下白斑；简历上一段空白让面试官皱眉
scene: 吸烟对健康有害。Smoking is detrimental to health.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：detrimental 指有害的；句意是吸烟对健康有害。

pos.zh: 有害的；损害的；造成伤害的

senses.title: Harmful to health or growth
senses.definition: causing harm to a person body or development
senses.definitionCN: 对人的身体或发育造成伤害
senses.example: Smoking is detrimental to health.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟对健康有害。
senses.why: A white mark left by a drop of acid on a table.
senses.whyCN: 一滴酸液在桌面上留下的白斑。

senses.title: Damaging to interests
senses.definition: having a bad effect on someone interests, rights or reputation
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的利益、权利或声誉产生不良影响
senses.example: The delay was detrimental to the project.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误对项目不利。
senses.why: A blank gap on a printed schedule.
senses.whyCN: 打印日程表上的一段空白。

senses.title: Harmful to a system
senses.definition: tending to weaken or damage an environment or organisation
senses.definitionCN: 倾向于削弱或损害环境或组织
senses.example: Runoff is detrimental to the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 径流对珊瑚礁有害。
senses.why: Cloudy water spreading over pale coral.
senses.whyCN: 浑浊的水漫过苍白的珊瑚。

intro.en: Detrimental comes from Latin detrimentum, loss or damage, from deterere, to wear away, de- down plus terere to rub.
intro.cn: detrimental 源自拉丁语 detrimentum（损失、损害），来自 deterere（磨损），由 de-（向下）加 terere（摩擦）构成。

items.en: Terere meant to rub.
items.cn: terere 意为摩擦。

items.en: Deterere meant to wear away by rubbing.
items.cn: deterere 意为磨掉。

items.en: Detrimentum meant the loss caused by wearing away.
items.cn: detrimentum 意为磨损造成的损失。

items.en: Detriment entered English for harm or loss.
items.cn: 十五世纪 detriment 以损害义进入英语。

items.en: Detrimental followed as the adjective.
items.cn: 十七世纪 detrimental 作为形容词随之出现。

items.en: It is standard in formal reports and law.
items.cn: 如今它是正式报告与法律中的标准用词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the ter- rub family; the near-meaning group names other words for causing harm.
note.cn: 形近组共享 ter-（摩擦）家族；近义组是其他表示「造成伤害」的词。

entries.definition: Harm or loss; it is the noun behind this adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 损害或损失；是这个形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: A gradual wearing down; it shares terere but names the process of rubbing away.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐消耗；共享 terere，但指磨掉的过程。

entries.definition: Overused and dull; it comes from tritus, worn by rubbing.
entries.definitionCN: 陈腐的；来自 tritus（被磨旧的）。

entries.definition: Likely to damage health or interests.
entries.definitionCN: 可能损害健康或利益。

entries.definition: Having a bad effect on something.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事物有不良影响。

entries.definition: Unfavourable and likely to cause problems.
entries.definitionCN: 不利的、可能带来问题的。

normalIntro.en: Detrimental is detriment- loss plus -al: like a surface worn away by rubbing, bit by bit.
normalIntro.cn: detrimental 就是 detriment-（损失）加 -al：像被摩擦一点点磨掉的表面。

normal.en: Ter- means rub, as in attrition.
normal.cn: ter- 意为摩擦，如 attrition。

normal.en: Detrimental takes to.
normal.cn: detrimental 后面接 to。

normal.en: Detriment is the noun, detrimental the adjective.
normal.cn: detriment 是名词，detrimental 是形容词。

normal.en: It is more formal than harmful.
normal.cn: 它比 harmful 更正式。

normal.en: Trite shares the worn root.
normal.cn: trite 共享「磨旧」这个词根。

abstract.en: A white mark left by a drop of acid on a table.
abstract.cn: 一滴酸液在桌面上留下的白斑。

abstract.en: A blank gap on a printed schedule.
abstract.cn: 打印日程表上的一段空白。

abstract.en: Cloudy water spreading over pale coral.
abstract.cn: 浑浊的水漫过苍白的珊瑚。

examples.en: Too much sun is detrimental to the skin.
examples.cn: 过多日晒对皮肤有害。

examples.en: The policy proved detrimental to small firms.
examples.cn: 这项政策结果证明对小公司不利。

examples.en: They listed the detrimental effects of noise.
examples.cn: 他们列出了噪音的种种危害。

dict_mnemonic.text: detrimental ＝ detriment（损害，拉丁语 de「向下」＋ terere「摩擦」→ deterere「磨损」）＋ -al（形容词后缀）＝像被磨掉一层那样造成损失，「有害的」。

root: 拉丁语 terere（摩擦）→ de-＋terere → deterere（磨损）→ detrimentum（损失）→ detriment → detrimental

sensesIntro.en: One surface worn away: a table, a schedule and a reef.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个被磨掉的表面：一张桌子、一份日程与一片珊瑚礁。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white mark left by a drop of acid on a polished table
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴酸液在擦亮的桌面上留下的白斑

branches.en: A white mark left by a drop of acid on a table.
branches.cn: 一滴酸液在桌面上留下的白斑。

branches.en: A blank gap on a printed schedule.
branches.cn: 打印日程表上的一段空白。

branches.en: Cloudy water spreading over pale coral.
branches.cn: 浑浊的水漫过苍白的珊瑚。

branches.en: Both leave a visible loss behind.
branches.cn: 两者都留下可见的损失。

branches.en: Both weaken something that was working well.
branches.cn: 两者都削弱原本运转良好的东西。

intro.en: Detrimental is de- plus ter- plus -al; the rub root also builds attrition and trite.
intro.cn: detrimental 由 de- 加 ter- 加 -al 构成；摩擦这个词根也造出 attrition 与 trite。

latinIntro.en: Latin terere means to rub, tritus worn and damnum loss.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 terere 意为摩擦，tritus 意为磨旧的，damnum 意为损失。

definition_zh: v. 使（货币）贬值；贬低；轻视（使显得不重要）
definition_en: to reduce the official exchange value of a currency, or to make something or someone seem less important
core_image: 汇率牌上数字一夜之间往下跳；一个人把别人的建议随手推到桌角
scene: 政府让货币贬值了。The government devalued the currency.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：devalued 指使贬值；句意是政府让货币贬值了。

senses.title: Lower a currency worth
senses.definition: to reduce the official exchange value of a currency
senses.definitionCN: 降低一种货币的官方兑换价值
senses.example: The government devalued the currency.
senses.exampleCN: 政府让货币贬值了。
senses.why: A rate board with the figure shifted down overnight.
senses.whyCN: 一块汇率牌，数字一夜之间被调低。

senses.title: Make something seem less worth
senses.definition: to make something appear less important or valuable
senses.definitionCN: 使某物显得不那么重要或有价值
senses.example: The comment devalued her research.
senses.exampleCN: 那条评论贬低了她的研究。
senses.why: A report pushed to the corner of a desk.
senses.whyCN: 一份被推到桌角的报告。

senses.title: Treat a person as less worth
senses.definition: to make a person feel that they are not valued
senses.definitionCN: 让一个人觉得自己不被重视
senses.example: He felt devalued by the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定让他觉得自己不被重视。
senses.why: A name badge left off a staff list.
senses.whyCN: 员工名单上被漏掉的一个姓名牌。

intro.en: Devalue is de- down plus value, from Old French valoir, from Latin valere, to be strong or worth.
intro.cn: devalue 由 de-（向下）加 value 构成；value 来自古法语 valoir，源自拉丁语 valere（强健、有价值）。

items.en: Valere meant to be strong or worth.
items.cn: valere 意为强健、有价值。

items.en: Valoir meant to be worth.
items.cn: 古法语 valoir 意为值得。

items.en: Value entered English for worth.
items.cn: 十五世纪 value 以价值义进入英语。

items.en: Devalue appeared for lowering value.
items.cn: 十九世纪 devalue 出现，表示降低价值。

items.en: Devaluation became a standard policy term.
items.cn: 二十世纪 devaluation 成为标准政策术语。

items.en: It now also covers belittling people.
items.cn: 如今它也用于描述贬低人。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the val- worth family; the near-meaning group names other ways of lowering worth.
note.cn: 形近组共享 val-（价值）家族；近义组是其他表示「降低价值」的词。

entries.definition: Worth, or to regard as important; devalue adds de- to push it down.
entries.definitionCN: 价值，或重视；devalue 加 de- 把它往下压。

entries.definition: To judge the worth of something; it shares valere but measures rather than lowers.
entries.definitionCN: 判断某物的价值；共享 valere，但是衡量而非降低。

entries.definition: The act of lowering a currency value.
entries.definitionCN: 降低币值的行为。

entries.definition: To lose value over time, especially by market forces.
entries.definitionCN: 随时间失去价值，尤指受市场力量影响。

entries.definition: To make someone or something seem unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人或某物显得不重要。

entries.definition: To move something to a lower level or rating.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物降到更低的级别或评级。

normalIntro.en: Devalue is de- down plus val- worth: move the worth down, on a board or in a mind.
normalIntro.cn: devalue 就是 de-（向下）加 val-（价值）：把价值往下移，无论是在牌子上还是在人心里。

normal.en: Val- means worth, as in value.
normal.cn: val- 意为价值，如 value。

normal.en: Devalue is deliberate; depreciate is often natural.
normal.cn: devalue 是人为的，depreciate 常是自然发生的。

normal.en: Devaluation is the noun for a currency.
normal.cn: devaluation 是用于货币的名词。

normal.en: Devalue their work means belittle it.
normal.cn: devalue their work 就是贬低他们的成果。

normal.en: Feel devalued means feel unimportant.
normal.cn: feel devalued 就是觉得自己不重要。

abstract.en: A rate board with the figure shifted down overnight.
abstract.cn: 一块汇率牌，数字一夜之间被调低。

abstract.en: A report pushed to the corner of a desk.
abstract.cn: 一份被推到桌角的报告。

abstract.en: A name badge left off a staff list.
abstract.cn: 员工名单上被漏掉的一个姓名牌。

examples.en: They devalued the pound by ten percent.
examples.cn: 他们让英镑贬值百分之十。

examples.en: Such remarks devalue the whole team.
examples.cn: 这类言论贬低了整个团队。

examples.en: The award was devalued by too many winners.
examples.cn: 获奖者太多，这个奖也就贬值了。

dict_mnemonic.text: devalue ＝ de（向下）＋ value（价值，拉丁语 valere「强健、值得」，与 valid、valuable 同根）＝把价值往下压，「使贬值、贬低」。

root: 拉丁语 valere（强健、有价值）→ 古法语 valoir → value（价值）→ de-＋value → devalue

sensesIntro.en: One figure moved down: a rate board, a pushed report and a missing name.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个被调低的数字：一块汇率牌、一份被推开的报告与一个被漏掉的名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rate board with the figure shifted down overnight
core.cn: 核心意象：一块汇率牌，数字一夜之间被调低

branches.en: A rate board with the figure shifted down overnight.
branches.cn: 一块汇率牌，数字一夜之间被调低。

branches.en: A report pushed to the corner of a desk.
branches.cn: 一份被推到桌角的报告。

branches.en: A name badge left off a staff list.
branches.cn: 员工名单上被漏掉的一个姓名牌。

branches.en: Both lower a stated worth.
branches.cn: 两者都降低一个被标出的价值。

branches.en: Both make a person feel smaller.
branches.cn: 两者都让人觉得自己变小了。

intro.en: Devalue is de- plus val-; the worth root also builds value, valid and evaluate.
intro.cn: devalue 由 de- 加 val- 构成；价值这个词根也造出 value、valid 与 evaluate。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere means to be strong, pretium a price and gradus a step.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere 意为强健，pretium 意为价格，gradus 意为台阶。

definition_zh: v. 毁坏；毁灭；使极为震惊悲痛；重创（经济等）
definition_en: to damage a place so badly that little is left, or to make someone feel very shocked and sad
core_image: 洪水退去后，整条街只剩地基；一个人读到消息，坐在椅子里很久没动
scene: 地震毁掉了整座城。The earthquake devastated the city.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：devastated 指毁坏；句意是地震毁掉了整座城。

pos.zh: 毁坏；毁灭；使极为震惊悲痛

senses.title: Destroy a place
senses.definition: to damage a place so badly that little is left
senses.definitionCN: 把一个地方损坏到几乎不剩什么
senses.example: The earthquake devastated the city.
senses.exampleCN: 地震毁掉了整座城。
senses.why: A street with only foundations left after a flood.
senses.whyCN: 洪水过后只剩地基的一条街。

senses.title: Shock a person deeply
senses.definition: to make someone feel very shocked and sad
senses.definitionCN: 使某人感到极度震惊与悲伤
senses.example: She was devastated by the news.
senses.exampleCN: 她被这个消息击垮了。
senses.why: A person sitting still in a chair holding a letter.
senses.whyCN: 一个人捏着信坐在椅子里一动不动。

senses.title: Ruin an economy or system
senses.definition: to cause severe damage to an economy, industry or habitat
senses.definitionCN: 对经济、行业或栖息地造成严重损害
senses.example: The drought devastated the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱毁掉了收成。
senses.why: A field of cracked earth with no crop.
senses.whyCN: 一片龟裂、没有庄稼的田地。

intro.en: Devastate comes from Latin devastare, de- completely plus vastare to lay waste, from vastus, empty or waste.
intro.cn: devastate 源自拉丁语 devastare，由 de-（彻底）加 vastare（使荒芜）构成，vastare 来自 vastus（空旷、荒芜）。

items.en: Vastus meant empty or waste.
items.cn: vastus 意为空旷、荒芜。

items.en: Vastare meant to lay waste.
items.cn: vastare 意为使成荒地。

items.en: Devastare meant to lay completely waste.
items.cn: devastare 意为彻底毁成荒地。

items.en: Devastate entered English for laying waste.
items.cn: 十七世纪 devastate 以毁坏义进入英语。

items.en: It gained the sense of overwhelming grief.
items.cn: 十九世纪获得令人极度悲痛的意思。

items.en: Devastating now also praises a sharp wit.
items.cn: 如今 devastating 也用来夸赞犀利的机智。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vast- waste family; the near-meaning group names other ways of ruining.
note.cn: 形近组共享 vast-（荒芜）家族；近义组是其他表示「毁坏」的词。

entries.definition: Very large in area; it shares vastus but describes empty size, not ruin.
entries.definitionCN: 面积极大的；共享 vastus，但描述空旷的大小而非毁坏。

entries.definition: Great destruction or shock.
entries.definitionCN: 巨大的破坏或震惊。

entries.definition: Causing great damage or shock.
entries.definitionCN: 造成巨大破坏或震惊的。

entries.definition: To damage something so it no longer exists or works.
entries.definitionCN: 损坏某物使其不再存在或运作。

entries.definition: To damage something severely.
entries.definitionCN: 严重毁坏某物。

entries.definition: To destroy or badly damage a thing or plan.
entries.definitionCN: 毁坏或严重损害某物或计划。

normalIntro.en: Devastate is de- fully plus vast- waste: make a place as empty as a wasteland.
normalIntro.cn: devastate 就是 de-（彻底）加 vast-（荒芜）：把一个地方变得像荒地一样空。

normal.en: Vast- means empty waste, not just big.
normal.cn: vast- 意为空旷荒芜，不只是大。

normal.en: Devastate a place, devastate a person.
normal.cn: devastate 既可指地方也可指人。

normal.en: Be devastated by is the common passive.
normal.cn: be devastated by 是常见被动搭配。

normal.en: Devastation is the noun of the ruin.
normal.cn: devastation 是毁坏的名词。

normal.en: Waste shares the same Latin root.
normal.cn: waste 共享同一拉丁词根。

abstract.en: A street with only foundations left after a flood.
abstract.cn: 洪水过后只剩地基的一条街。

abstract.en: A person sitting still in a chair holding a letter.
abstract.cn: 一个人捏着信坐在椅子里一动不动。

abstract.en: A field of cracked earth with no crop.
abstract.cn: 一片龟裂、没有庄稼的田地。

examples.en: The fire devastated three villages.
examples.cn: 大火毁掉了三个村庄。

examples.en: He was devastated when the team lost.
examples.cn: 球队输了，他极为难过。

examples.en: Pollution has devastated the river life.
examples.cn: 污染毁掉了河里的生物。

dict_mnemonic.text: devastate ＝ de（彻底）＋ vast（空旷、荒芜，拉丁语 vastus；vast「广阔的」同根）＋ -ate（动词后缀）＝彻底变成荒地，「毁坏」。

root: 拉丁语 vastus（空旷、荒芜）→ vastare（使成荒地）→ de-＋vastare → devastare → 英语 devastate

sensesIntro.en: One place emptied: a street, a chair with a letter and a cracked field.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个被清空的地方：一条街、一把捏着信的椅子与一片龟裂的田。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street with only foundations left after the flood water went down
core.cn: 核心意象：洪水退去后只剩地基的一条街

branches.en: A street with only foundations left after a flood.
branches.cn: 洪水过后只剩地基的一条街。

branches.en: A person sitting still in a chair holding a letter.
branches.cn: 一个人捏着信坐在椅子里一动不动。

branches.en: A field of cracked earth with no crop.
branches.cn: 一片龟裂、没有庄稼的田地。

branches.en: Both leave a place with nothing usable.
branches.cn: 两者都让一个地方不剩可用之物。

branches.en: Both take away what someone relied on.
branches.cn: 两者都夺走某人依靠的东西。

intro.en: Devastate is de- plus vast- plus -ate; the waste root also builds vast and devastation.
intro.cn: devastate 由 de- 加 vast- 加 -ate 构成；荒芜这个词根也造出 vast 与 devastation。

latinIntro.en: Latin vastus means empty, vastare to lay waste and ruere to fall.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vastus 意为空旷，vastare 意为使成荒地，ruere 意为倒塌。

definition_zh: 发展；显影；培养；开发
definition_en: to grow or to make something grow into a larger, fuller or better form
core_image: 一张卷起的底片浸进药水，影像一点点显出来
scene: 暗房里红灯亮着，白纸在水盘里轻轻晃，山影慢慢浮上来。The image began to develop after a few seconds.
sceneCN: 这里 develop 指「显影」（第 2 个义项：影像在药水里渐渐显出）；句意是几秒之后影像开始显出来。

senses.title: Grow into a larger form
senses.definition: to grow or change into something bigger or more advanced
senses.definitionCN: 成长或变化为更大、更先进的样子
senses.example: The small town developed into a busy port.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小镇发展成了一座繁忙的港口。
senses.why: Nothing is built in one day; the shape arrives in layers.
senses.whyCN: 没有东西是一天建成的，形状是一层层到来的。

senses.title: Become visible on film
senses.definition: to become visible on film or paper through a chemical process
senses.definitionCN: 通过化学过程在胶片或相纸上显现出来
senses.example: The image began to develop after a few seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 几秒之后影像开始显出来。
senses.why: The picture was already on the film, waiting for the liquid.
senses.whyCN: 画面早已在底片上，只等着那盘药水。

senses.title: Build up a skill or habit
senses.definition: to gradually acquire a skill, habit or quality
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐获得一种技能、习惯或品质
senses.example: Children develop language skills very quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童培养语言技能非常快。
senses.why: A skill grows the way a plant does, by small daily additions.
senses.whyCN: 技能的生长像植物，靠每天一点点加上去。

intro.en: Develop comes from French desveloper, to unwrap, built from des- and a word for wrapping, and English took it up in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: develop 来自法语 desveloper（打开包裹），由 des- 与表示包裹的词根构成，十七世纪进入英语。

items.en: Desveloper meant to unwrap something that had been rolled up.
items.cn: desveloper 指把卷起来包好的东西打开。

items.en: French developper added the sense of unfolding over time.
items.cn: 法语 developper 又添上「随时间慢慢展开」的意思。

items.en: English develop first meant to bring out what was hidden.
items.cn: 英语 develop 最初指把藏着的东西带出来。

items.en: Photography gave it the sense of an image appearing in liquid.
items.cn: 摄影让它带上影像在药水里浮现的意思。

items.en: It now covers growth, skills, land and new products.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖成长、技能、土地与新产品。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the develop stem, while the meaning group moves from growing to widening and evolving.
note.cn: 形近组共用 develop 这个词干，近义组则从生长走到扩张与演变。

entries.definition: the process of growing or improving
entries.definitionCN: 成长或改进的过程

entries.definition: a person or company that builds things
entries.definitionCN: 建造事物的人或公司

entries.definition: relating to growth and change
entries.definitionCN: 与成长变化有关的

entries.definition: to become larger over time
entries.definitionCN: 随着时间变得更大

entries.definition: to become wider or more extensive
entries.definitionCN: 变得更宽或范围更大

entries.definition: to change slowly into a different form
entries.definitionCN: 慢慢变成另一种形态

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a film curled inside its roll and end with a child learning words.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从胶卷里卷着的底片开始，落到一个学说话的孩子。

normal.en: To develop is first to unwrap, then to let the shape appear.
normal.cn: develop 先解开包裹，再让形状自己出现。

normal.en: A town and a photograph both need time in the bath.
normal.cn: 小镇与照片，都需要在药水里泡够时间。

normal.en: A habit is built from days that look almost the same.
normal.cn: 习惯是用一个又一个看起来差不多的日子搭起来的。

normal.en: Nothing shouts while it develops; growth is quiet work.
normal.cn: 发展中的东西从不喊，成长是安静的工作。

normal.en: The negative holds the picture before the eye can see it.
normal.cn: 在眼睛看见之前，底片就已经握着那幅画面。

abstract.en: Picture a dark room lit only by a red lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象一间只亮着红灯的暗房。

abstract.en: Picture a hand rocking a tray of liquid slowly.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手慢慢摇动一盘药水。

abstract.en: Picture a child repeating one new word all afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子整个下午反复念一个新词。

examples.en: The small town developed into a busy port.
examples.cn: 这个小镇发展成了一座繁忙的港口。

examples.en: Children develop language skills very quickly.
examples.cn: 儿童培养语言技能非常快。

examples.en: The film needs ten minutes to develop properly.
examples.cn: 底片需要十分钟才能正常显影。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 develop 记成「地维勒普」：de 是打开，velop 像卷起的包裹，把包裹打开，东西就一点点发展、显出来。

root: 来自古法语 desveloper，由 des-（打开）与表示包裹的词根组成，本义是解开卷起的东西，十七世纪进入英语。从「展开」引申为事物逐渐成长成形，再用于摄影显影、技能培养与土地开发。

sensesIntro.en: From a wrapped thing opened out, to a picture rising in liquid, to a skill built day by day.
sensesIntro.cn: 从包着的东西被打开，到画面在药水里浮起，再到一天天搭起的技能。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something rolled up slowly opening into a full picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：卷起的东西慢慢展开成一幅完整的画面。

branches.en: The first sense is a place or thing opening into a bigger form.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是一个地方或事物展开成更大的样子。

branches.en: The second sense is a picture opening out of blank film.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一幅画从空白底片里展开。

branches.en: The third sense is a skill unfolding inside a person.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一种技能在一个人身上展开。

branches.en: A town and a photograph both reveal a shape that was waiting.
branches.cn: 小镇与照片，都在显出一个早已等着的形状。

branches.en: Places and people develop by the same slow unfolding.
branches.cn: 地方和人，都是靠同一种缓慢展开而发展。

intro.en: Develop grows a large family around unwrapping, growth and building.
intro.cn: develop 长出一大族词，围绕展开、成长与建设。

latinIntro.en: The French base means to unwrap, and the modern family keeps that picture of something opening out.

items.example: Development of the site began in May.
items.exampleCN: 这块地的开发五月开始。

items.example: The developer showed us the plans.
items.exampleCN: 开发商给我们看了图纸。
这是一个发展中的市场。

definition_zh: 越轨；偏离社会规范的行为；（统计）偏差；（对标准的）偏离
definition_en: behaviour or a value that departs from accepted norms, standards or expected patterns
core_image: 一条笔直的车辙延伸到岔路口，一辆车忽然拐出主路，压进旁边的草地
scene: 大路中间有两道笔直的车辙，一辆车在岔口忽然拐出主路，压进旁边的草地。Sociologists ask why some forms of deviance are punished and others are ignored.
sceneCN: 这里指「违反社会规范的越轨行为」（第 1 个义项：对社会规范的偏离行为）；句意为社会学家追问为什么有些越轨受到惩罚，另一些却被忽视。可辨识物件：车辙、岔路口、草地、路牌、车轮。

pos.zh: 越轨；偏离社会规范的行为（常作不可数）

derivatives.zh: 迂回的；狡诈的（同出「离开大路」词根）

senses.title: Behaviour that breaks a social norm
senses.definition: conduct that violates the accepted rules or expectations of a society or group
senses.definitionCN: 违反一个社会或群体公认规则或期待的行为
senses.example: Sociologists ask why some forms of deviance are punished and others are ignored.
senses.exampleCN: 社会学家追问为什么有些越轨受到惩罚，另一些却被忽视。
senses.why: The Latin verb means 'to turn off the road'; deviance is behaviour that leaves the path everyone else follows.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「拐离道路」；越轨就是离开众人所走那条路的行为。

senses.title: A statistical measure of misfit
senses.titleCN: 统计上衡量拟合偏差的量
senses.definition: a quantity that measures how far a model or observation departs from an expected pattern
senses.definitionCN: 衡量模型或观测偏离预期格局多远的量
senses.example: The model's deviance fell sharply after the new term was added.
senses.exampleCN: 加入新项之后，模型的偏差值急剧下降。
senses.why: Statistics kept the road image: a point far from the fitted line is a car far from the tracks.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留了这个道路意象：远离拟合线的点，就像远离车辙的车。

senses.title: A breach that can clarify the rules
senses.titleCN: 反而能澄清规范的越轨
senses.definition: the sociological idea that violation can mark the boundary of what a society considers normal
senses.definitionCN: 越轨可以标出一个社会视为正常的边界这一社会学观念
senses.example: Durkheim argued that deviance can clarify a society's norms.
senses.exampleCN: 涂尔干认为，越轨能够澄清一个社会的规范。
senses.why: A line is easiest to see when someone steps over it, so the breach itself draws the boundary.
senses.whyCN: 有人越过界线时，界线才最容易看清，因此越轨本身把边界画了出来。

senses.title: A violation written into law
senses.definition: behaviour that breaks a formal rule carrying a legal penalty, usually called crime
senses.definitionCN: 违反带有法律惩罚的正式规则的行为，通常称为犯罪
senses.example: Formal deviance includes offences written into the criminal code.
senses.exampleCN: 正式越轨包括写进刑法典的罪行。
senses.why: When a society writes its norms into a code, stepping off the road becomes a punishable act.
senses.whyCN: 当一个社会把规范写进法典，离开道路就变成可受惩罚的行为。

senses.title: A small breach of manners
senses.definition: a minor violation of everyday expectations that draws disapproval but no legal charge
senses.definitionCN: 对日常期待的轻微违背，招来不满却不会带来法律指控
senses.example: Informal deviance, such as queue-jumping, draws stares rather than charges.
senses.exampleCN: 非正式越轨，比如插队，招来的是白眼而不是指控。
senses.why: Not every departure from the road is a crime; some only cause others to look up.
senses.whyCN: 并非每次离开道路都是犯罪；有些只让旁人抬起头看一眼。

senses.title: A breach amplified by attention
senses.titleCN: 因关注而被放大的越轨
senses.definition: the process in which publicity and moral panic make a small deviation seem larger and more common
senses.definitionCN: 宣传与道德恐慌使一个小的偏离显得更大、更常见的过程
senses.example: Sensational coverage produced deviance amplification in the following months.
senses.exampleCN: 耸动的报道在随后几个月里造成了越轨放大。
senses.why: Attention works like a lens: the same small swerve can be magnified until it fills the frame.
senses.whyCN: 关注就像镜头：同一个轻微拐弯可以被放大到填满画面。

senses.title: A stigmatizing label from the past
senses.titleCN: 带有污名色彩的旧标签
senses.definition: an older clinical or moral label applied to behaviour that later generations regard as ordinary
senses.definitionCN: 旧时贴在后来被视为平常的行为上的临床或道德标签
senses.example: The old manual used deviance to pathologize behaviour now accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 旧手册用「越轨」把如今被接受的行为病理化。
senses.why: The word can be a verdict as well as a description, and old verdicts often say more about the judge than the accused.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既可以是描述，也可以是判决，而旧判决常常更多说明判者而非被判定者。

senses.title: Distance from a technical standard
senses.definition: the amount by which a measurement, product or process differs from a stated standard
senses.definitionCN: 测量值、产品或流程与规定标准之间的差距
senses.example: The lab recorded any deviance from the calibration standard.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室记录了任何与校准标准的偏离。
senses.why: In a laboratory the road is a calibration line, and deviance is how far the reading has wandered from it.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，道路就是一条校准线，而偏差是读数偏离它多远。

intro.en: Deviance comes from Latin deviare 'to turn off the road', built on de- 'away' and via 'way, road'. The English noun was formed from deviant and established in sociology in the twentieth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: deviance 来自拉丁 deviare「拐离道路」，由 de-「离开」与 via「道路」构成。这个英语名词由 deviant 构成，并在二十世纪的社会学中确立。年代均为约数。

items.en: Via meant 'way, road, path'. Its deeper origin is not established; the road root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: via 意为「道路、路径」。其更深来源未得到证明；为它提出的「道路」词根属于重构形式。

items.en: De- 'away' plus via produced deviare, 'to leave the road, turn aside'.
items.cn: de-「离开」加 via 构成 deviare「离开道路、拐向一旁」。

items.en: The participle devians named someone or something in the act of turning off the road.
items.cn: 分词 devians 指正在拐离道路的人或物。

items.en: English adopted the verb and adjective in the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries, first in the literal sense of straying from a route.
items.cn: 英语在十五与十六世纪引入动词与形容词，最初用的是「偏离路线」的字面义。

items.en: The noun deviance was formed from deviant with the ending -ance and became a standard sociological term in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 名词 deviance 由 deviant 加名词后缀构成，在二十世纪成为标准的社会学术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin source of via is unsettled, and no exact first citation is fixed for the statistical sense, so dates here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：via 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论；统计义也没有确切的最早书证，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds the same off-the-road family; group two holds terms for departure from a norm or pattern.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「拐离道路」词族的词；第二组是表示偏离规范或格局的术语。

entries.definition: Describing behaviour that departs from norms, or a person who does so; deviance names the phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 描述偏离规范的行为，或这样的人；deviance 指这一现象本身。

entries.definition: To depart from a route, standard or expected course; the noun is the result of doing so.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离路线、标准或预期方向；名词是这一动作的结果。

entries.definition: A departure from an expected value or course; it is neutral in tone, while deviance often carries a social judgement.
entries.definitionCN: 对预期值或路线的偏离；语气中立，而 deviance 常带社会评判。

entries.definition: Means indirect or cunning, literally 'off the main road'; it shares the root without the sociological sense.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「迂回的、狡诈的」，字面是「离开大路」；共享词根，却无社会学含义。

entries.definition: Refusal to take the shape a group expects; it often suggests choice, while deviance can be statistical or unintended.
entries.definitionCN: 拒绝采取群体期待的形状；常暗示主动选择，而 deviance 可以是统计性的或非故意的。

entries.definition: Minor criminal behaviour, especially by young people; it is a legal category, narrower than deviance.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微的犯罪行为，尤指青少年所为；它是法律类别，比 deviance 更窄。

entries.definition: A thing that does not match the expected pattern; it can be neutral and has no moral weight.
entries.definitionCN: 不符合预期格局的事物；可以完全中立，不带道德重量。

entries.definition: A single departure from normal behaviour or expectation, often brief and unusual.
entries.definitionCN: 对正常行为或预期的一次偏离，通常短暂而少见。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real road root, the real derivatives and the real sociological phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「道路」词根、真实的派生词与真实的社会学搭配。

normal.en: The Latin verb means 'to turn off the road', so every sense is some kind of departure from a line.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为「拐离道路」，因此每个义项都是对某条线的一种偏离。

normal.en: The family runs deviate, deviant, deviance, deviation, deviously and devious.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 deviate、deviant、deviance、deviation、deviously 与 devious。

normal.en: The sociological phrases are social deviance, the study of deviance and deviance amplification.
normal.cn: 社会学搭配有社会越轨、越轨研究与越轨放大。

normal.en: The measurement phrases are measure deviance and deviance from the norm.
normal.cn: 测量搭配有测量偏差与对规范的偏离。

normal.en: The adjective deviant is the person or behaviour, while the noun names the pattern they make.
normal.cn: 形容词 deviant 指人或行为，名词则指它们形成的模式。

abstract.en: Picture a car leaving two straight tracks and pressing into the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车离开两道笔直的车辙，压进草地。

abstract.en: Picture a point on a graph that sits far from every fitted line.
abstract.cn: 想象图上一个点远离所有拟合线。

abstract.en: Picture a small swerve on the evening news, magnified until it fills the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象晚间新闻里一个轻微拐弯，被放大到填满屏幕。

examples.en: The course compares deviance in different legal systems.
examples.cn: 这门课程比较不同法律体系中的越轨现象。

examples.en: A single deviance in the reading was enough to stop the batch.
examples.cn: 读数中仅仅一处偏差就足以让这批产品停下。

examples.en: The label of deviance often tells us more about who held the pen than about the person described.
examples.cn: 「越轨」这个标签常常更多说明谁握着笔，而非被描述的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离开」加「道路」——别人沿大路走，他拐进草地 → 越轨、偏离

root: deviance 来自拉丁 deviare「拐离道路」= de-「离开」+ via「道路」；英语名词由 deviant 加名词后缀构成。via 在拉丁语之前的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: leaving the expected line. The movement is applied to social norms, a statistical fit, the boundary of rules, criminal law, everyday manners, media attention, an old moral label and a technical standard.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：离开预期的那条线。这个动作依次用于社会规范、统计拟合、规范边界、刑法、日常礼俗、媒体关注、旧道德标签与技术标准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a car turning out of two straight tracks into the grass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆车从两道笔直的车辙拐进草地。

branches.en: THE FIRST SWERVE: behaviour leaves the path that the group treats as normal.
branches.cn: 第一次拐弯：行为离开了群体视为正常的那条路。

branches.en: THE MEASURED DISTANCE: a statistical model and a calibration standard both turn the road into a number.
branches.cn: 被测量的距离：统计模型与校准标准都把道路变成一个数字。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE BOUNDARY: the breach itself shows where the line had been all along.
branches.cn: 可见的边界：越轨本身显示出界线一直所在的位置。

branches.en: THE TWO CODES: criminal law punishes the large swerve, while manners only register the small one.
branches.cn: 两套法典：刑法惩罚大幅拐弯，礼俗只记录轻微拐弯。

branches.en: THE LENS AND THE LABEL: attention magnifies the swerve, and an old label decides whose swerve it is.
branches.cn: 镜头与标签：关注放大拐弯，旧标签则决定这是谁的拐弯。

intro.en: The noun can be read from a Latin prefix of departure, the Latin noun for a road, the verb built on them and the derived family.
intro.cn: 这个名词可以按表示离开的拉丁前缀、表示道路的拉丁名词、由它们构成的动词以及派生词族逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin de- and via give deviare; English built deviate, deviant and deviance on the same stem, and devious keeps the literal image of being off the road.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 de- 与 via 构成 deviare；英语在同一词干上构成 deviate、deviant 与 deviance，而 devious 保留了「离开大路」的字面意象。

items.example: The prefix marks movement away from the path.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记离开道路的移动。

items.example: The noun supplies the image of a travelled route.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供被行走的路线意象。

items.example: The Latin verb named leaving the route.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词指离开路线。

items.example: The aircraft deviated from its flight path.

items.meaning: a departure from an expected value
items.example: The gauge showed a small deviation.
items.exampleCN: 仪表显示出一处小偏差。

items.example: The study followed deviant behaviour in adolescents.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究追踪青少年的越轨行为。

items.meaning: the state or pattern of departing from norms
items.example: Deviance is defined by the group that judges it.
items.exampleCN: 越轨由作出评判的群体来定义。

items.example: The machine behaved deviantly under load.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器在负载下出现了偏离行为。

items.example: The route was devious but safe.

definition_zh: 偏离；偏差；背离；绕航
definition_en: a departure from an established course, standard or expected value
core_image: 一辆车从笔直的路上拐出，轮胎压到旁边的草地
scene: 流程卡上有一步被跳过，箭头拐出了既定路线：A small deviation from the standard procedure caused the sample to fail.
sceneCN: 这里 deviation 是「偏离」（第 1 个义项：离开既定规程）；句意：稍微偏离标准流程就导致样本不合格。图中可辨识物件：流程卡、偏离的箭头、报废样本、记录表。

senses.title: Departing from a set course
senses.titleCN: 偏离：不走规定的那条路
senses.definition: the act of moving away from an established plan, rule or course
senses.definitionCN: 离开既定计划、规则或路线的行为
senses.example: Any deviation from the safety checklist must be recorded.
senses.exampleCN: 任何偏离安全检查表的行为都必须记录。
senses.why: deviare is de- 'off' plus via 'road'. A deviation is literally a step off the road, so the standard is the road left behind.
senses.whyCN: deviare 是 de-“离开”加 via“道路”。deviation 字面上就是走出道路，因此标准就是被留在身后的那条路。

senses.title: Distance from a statistical mean
senses.titleCN: 统计偏差：离平均值有多远
senses.definition: the difference between a value and a reference value such as a mean
senses.definitionCN: 某个值与平均值等参照值之间的差
senses.example: The standard deviation shows how widely the scores spread.
senses.exampleCN: 标准差显示分数分散得有多开。
senses.why: Statistics draws a straight line through the data, the mean, and calls every departure from it a deviation. The road becomes an average.
senses.whyCN: 统计学在数据中画出一条直线——平均值，并把每个离开它的点称为 deviation。道路变成了平均值。

senses.title: Compass error
senses.definition: the angle by which a compass needle is deflected from magnetic north by nearby metal or electric fields
senses.definitionCN: 指南针因附近金属或电场偏离磁北的角度
senses.example: The ship's compass had a deviation of four degrees near the engine room.
senses.exampleCN: 在机舱附近，船上的罗盘有四周的偏差。
senses.why: A needle wants to follow one line but is pulled off it by local iron. The word names the angle between the intended line and the actual one.
senses.whyCN: 指针本想沿一条线，却被附近的铁拉离。这个词命名预期线与实际线之间的夹角。

senses.title: Leaving the planned route
senses.titleCN: 绕航：船或飞机临时改路
senses.definition: the departure of a ship or aircraft from its declared route
senses.definitionCN: 船只或飞机离开申报航线的行为
senses.example: The aircraft reported a deviation to avoid the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机报告为避开风暴而偏离航线。
senses.why: Navigation makes the road metaphor literal: a course is drawn on a chart, and any other path is a deviation, even a safe one.
senses.whyCN: 导航让道路隐喻变成字面：航线画在海图上，任何别的路径都是 deviation，即使是为了安全。

senses.title: Behaviour departing from a norm
senses.titleCN: 越轨：行为离开群体规范
senses.definition: behaviour that departs from the accepted norms of a group or society
senses.definitionCN: 离开群体或社会公认规范的行为
senses.example: Sociologists study how groups define deviation and punish it.
senses.exampleCN: 社会学家研究群体如何界定并惩罚越轨行为。
senses.why: Here the road is a social norm. The word is descriptive of the departure, though it often carries the group's disapproval.
senses.whyCN: 这里的道路是社会规范。这个词描述偏离本身，但常带着群体的不认可。

senses.title: Manufacturing tolerance gap
senses.titleCN: 公差偏差：零件差了多少
senses.definition: the amount by which a manufactured part differs from its specified size
senses.definitionCN: 制造零件与其规定尺寸相差的量
senses.example: Parts with a deviation greater than 0.1 mm are rejected.
senses.exampleCN: 偏差超过 0.1 毫米的零件会被拒收。
senses.why: A specification is the intended road, and the finished part may sit slightly off it. The noun measures that gap in millimetres.
senses.whyCN: 规格是预期道路，成品零件可能略微偏离。这个名词用毫米测量那道缝。

senses.title: A physical bend from normal
senses.definition: in medicine, a displacement of a body part from its normal position
senses.definitionCN: 医学上身体某部位偏离正常位置
senses.example: A septal deviation can make breathing difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 鼻中隔偏斜会让呼吸变得困难。
senses.why: The body has an expected alignment, and the structure leaves it. The medical use keeps the geometric sense of an angle off the normal line.
senses.whyCN: 身体有预期的对齐线，结构离开它。医学用法保留了偏离正常线的几何含义。

senses.title: A deliberate exception
senses.titleCN: 例外偏离：经批准的破例
senses.definition: an approved departure from a rule or procedure in a specific case
senses.definitionCN: 在特定情况下经批准离开规则或程序
senses.example: The regulator granted a deviation for the older equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 监管机构对较旧设备批准了一项偏离许可。
senses.why: A deviation can be authorised: the road is left on purpose and the departure is written down. The noun then names the exception rather than the fault.
senses.whyCN: deviation 可以是获准的：有意离开道路，并把偏离写下来。此时名词命名的是例外，而非过错。

intro.en: Deviation comes from Latin deviatio, from deviare 'to turn off the road', de- 'off' plus via 'way'. English borrowed it through French; the statistical and compass senses are later specialisations.
intro.cn: deviation 来自拉丁 deviatio，来自 deviare“离开道路”，由 de-“离开”和 via“道路”构成。英语经法语借入；统计义与罗盘义是后来的专门化。

items.en: via meant 'way, road, path'. It also gives viaduct, obvious (ob- 'in the way') and previous (prae- 'before' + via), so the family is about routes.
items.cn: via 意为“路、道路、路径”。它还派生了 viaduct、obvious（ob-“在路上”）、previous（prae-“在前”+ via），因此这个词族关乎路线。

items.en: deviare is de- 'off' plus viare 'to travel', giving 'to leave the road, stray'. Classical Latin used it for both physical wandering and moral straying.
items.cn: deviare 是 de-“离开”加 viare“行走”，意为“离开道路、走偏”。古典拉丁语既用它表示实际迷路，也表示道德偏离。

items.en: deviatio named the act of turning aside. The stem deviat- passes through French into English, where the noun is recorded from the 17th century; exact dating is uncertain.
items.cn: deviatio 命名转向一旁的动作。deviat- 词干经法语进入英语，名词记录于 17 世纪，确切年代存疑。

items.en: In the 18th century, navigation and magnetism gave deviation a precise technical sense: the angle between the intended course and the actual one.
items.cn: 18 世纪，航海与磁学给 deviation 一个精确的技术义：预期航向与实际航向之间的夹角。

items.en: In the 19th century, statistics named the distance of a value from a mean a deviation, and standard deviation became the standard measure of spread.
items.cn: 19 世纪，统计学把某个值到平均值的距离称为 deviation，standard deviation 成为衡量分散程度的标准量。

items.en: Sociology in the 20th century adopted deviation and deviance for behaviour that leaves accepted norms. The road became a social expectation.
items.cn: 20 世纪社会学采用 deviation 与 deviance 表示离开公认规范的行为。道路变成了社会期待。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the via root with different endings; the near-meaning group separates departure, divergence, discrepancy and variance.
note.cn: 形近组共享 via 词根、词尾不同；近义组区分偏离、分歧、不符与方差。

entries.definition: to leave a course or standard; the verb names the act, deviation names the result.
entries.definitionCN: 离开路线或标准；动词命名动作，deviation 命名结果。

entries.definition: departing from accepted norms; it often labels the actor rather than the gap.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离公认规范的；它常标记行为人，而不是差距本身。

entries.definition: winding, indirect, or deceitful. From devius 'off the road', the physical sense became a moral one.
entries.definitionCN: 迂回的；狡猾的。来自 devius“离开道路”，物理义转为道德义。

entries.definition: the act of leaving, or a change from a previous course; broader than deviation, which implies a standard to deviate from.
entries.definitionCN: 离开，或对先前路线的改变；比 deviation 宽，后者暗含有可偏离的标准。

entries.definition: the process of separating and going in different directions; it describes two lines moving apart, not one leaving a norm.
entries.definitionCN: 分开并朝不同方向走的过程；它描述两条线分开，而不是一条线离开规范。

entries.definition: a difference between things that should agree, such as two records; it compares two items rather than a value and a standard.
entries.definitionCN: 本应一致的事物之间的差异，如两份记录；它比较两个项目，而不是数值与标准。

entries.definition: the average squared deviation from the mean; it squares deviations to measure overall spread.
entries.definitionCN: 各值偏离平均值的平方的平均；它把偏差平方以衡量总体分散。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配和真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'off' + via 'road': deviation is stepping off the road.
normal.cn: de-“离开”+ via“道路”：deviation 就是走出道路。

normal.en: viaduct, obvious and previous all contain via; the family is a set of routes.
normal.cn: viaduct、obvious、previous 都含 via，这个词族是一组路线。

normal.en: The statistical fixed phrase is standard deviation, the standard measure of spread.
normal.cn: 统计固定短语是 standard deviation，即分散程度的标准量。

normal.en: In navigation, a deviation is an angle, not a mistake: it can be measured in degrees.
normal.cn: 在航海中，deviation 是一个角度而不是错误：可以用度数测量。

normal.en: Sociology pairs deviation with norm: without a norm, there is nothing to deviate from.
normal.cn: 社会学把 deviation 与 norm 配对：没有规范，就无从偏离。

abstract.en: Think of a car crossing the white line for a moment and then returning.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车短暂越过白线，然后又回到车道。

abstract.en: Think of a fence post leaning a few degrees out of line with the others.
abstract.cn: 想象一根栅栏柱比其余柱子歪了几度。

abstract.en: Think of a hiker cutting across a field while the path bends the other way.
abstract.cn: 想象小路向另一边弯，而徒步者直接穿过田野。

examples.en: The auditor found several deviations from the approved accounting procedure.
examples.cn: 审计员发现了几处偏离已批准会计程序的做法。

examples.en: A deviation of two degrees in the compass was enough to worry the captain.
examples.cn: 罗盘两度的偏差就足以让船长担心。

examples.en: The study measured deviation from the mean for each participant.
examples.cn: 这项研究测量了每位参与者偏离平均值的程度。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地via神”——地（de）上离开 via（路）走偏了，就像偏神 → deviation 偏离、偏差

root: 拉丁 deviare“离开道路”（de-“离开”+ via“路”）；deviat- 词干 + -ion 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one geometry: a line is drawn as the expected path, and the actual path is measured by how far it sits off that line.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一套几何：先画出一条预期路线，再测量实际路线偏离它多远。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vehicle leaving a straight road and touching the grass beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：车辆离开直路，压到旁边的草地。

branches.en: THE EXCEPTION: leaving the rule with permission is the same geometry with different paperwork.
branches.cn: 例外：获准违规是同一套几何配另一份文件。

branches.en: NUMBERS AND PARTS: a score off the mean and a part off its spec are both gaps measured from a reference line.
branches.cn: 数值与零件：偏离平均的分数与偏离规格的零件，都是从参照线量出的缝。

branches.en: COMPASS AND COURSE: a needle pulled aside and an aircraft off its route are the navigational form of the same angle.
branches.cn: 罗盘与航向：被拉偏的指针与偏离航线的飞机，是同一角度的导航形态。

branches.en: SOCIETY AND BODY: behaviour off a norm and a structure off its alignment both show a line that did not hold.
branches.cn: 社会与身体：偏离规范的行为与偏离对齐的身体结构，都显示一条没有守住的线。

branches.en: THE BASE GEOMETRY: every sense needs two lines, one intended and one actual, and measures the space between.
branches.cn: 基础几何：每个义项都需要两条线——一条预期的、一条实际的——并测量其间的距离。

intro.en: Deviation is deviat- plus -ion. Latin de- and via are fused inside the stem; English adds -ion, -ate, -ant and -ance productively.
intro.cn: deviation 是 deviat- 加 -ion。拉丁 de- 与 via 已融合在词干内；英语能产地加 -ion、-ate、-ant、-ance。

latinIntro.en: Latin via 'road' yields deviare 'leave the road', devius 'off the road', and deviatio 'a turning aside'. English relatives include deviate, deviant, devious and viaduct.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 via“路”派生 deviare“离开道路”、devius“离开道路的”、deviatio“转向一旁”。英语同族词包括 deviate、deviant、devious、viaduct。

items.meaning: to leave a course or standard
items.meaningCN: 偏离；背离（de-“离开”+ viare“行走”）
items.example: The pilot deviated to avoid the storm.
items.exampleCN: 飞行员为避开风暴而偏离航线。

items.meaning: a departure from a course or standard
items.meaningCN: 偏离；偏差（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: The deviation was within the allowed range.

items.meaningCN: 越轨的；异常者（-ant 构成形容词或人物名词）
items.example: The study examined deviant behaviour in groups.
items.exampleCN: 这项研究考察群体中的越轨行为。

items.meaning: the state of departing from norms
items.meaningCN: 越轨；偏离状态（-ance 构成状态名词）
items.example: Deviance is defined differently by each community.
items.exampleCN: 每个社群对越轨的定义都不同。

items.meaningCN: 迂回的；狡猾的（de-“离开”+ via“路”+ -ous）
items.example: They took a devious route through the hills.
items.exampleCN: 他们沿一条迂回路线穿过丘陵。

items.meaning: one that deviates, or a deflecting device
items.meaningCN: 偏离者；偏转装置（-or 构成施事者名词）
items.example: The flow deviator kept the stream away from the wall.
items.exampleCN: 导流装置使水流远离墙壁。

items.meaning: a bridge carrying a road across a valley
items.meaningCN: 高架桥；跨谷道路（via“路”+ ductus“引导”）
items.example: The old viaduct still carries the railway.
items.exampleCN: 那座旧高架桥仍承载着铁路。

items.meaning: so clear that it meets you in the road
items.meaningCN: 明显的（ob-“在路上”+ via“路”，原指挡在路前、迎面可见）
items.example: The error was obvious to everyone.
items.exampleCN: 这个错误对所有人来说都显而易见。

latinEntries.meaning: to leave the road; to stray

definition_zh: 装置；设备；手段；手法
definition_en: a machine or tool made for a particular purpose
core_image: 桌上一个拆开的小机器，线圈和齿轮裸露在外
scene: 他拧开外壳，里面的线圈和齿轮露出来，桌上散着小螺丝。The device measures the moisture in the soil.
sceneCN: 这里 device 指「装置」（第 1 个义项：为特定用途做的小机器）；句意是这个装置测量土壤里的湿度。

senses.title: A piece of equipment
senses.definition: a machine or tool made for a particular job
senses.definitionCN: 为某项特定工作而制造的机器或工具
senses.example: The device measures the moisture in the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这个装置测量土壤里的湿度。
senses.why: Human hands cannot stay in the field all year, so a small machine does.
senses.whyCN: 人的手没法整年守在田里，于是让一台小机器守着。

senses.title: A method or trick
senses.definition: a plan or trick used to get a particular result
senses.definitionCN: 为得到某个结果而用的计策或花招
senses.example: Silence was just a device to make us talk.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默只是一种让我们开口的手段。
senses.why: A plan can work like a tool even when it has no parts.
senses.whyCN: 一个计策即使没有零件，也能像工具那样起作用。

senses.title: A literary technique
senses.definition: a particular way of writing that produces a chosen effect
senses.definitionCN: 为产生某种效果而采用的特定写法
senses.example: The writer uses repetition as a poetic device.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家把重复当作一种诗歌手法。
senses.why: Words can be arranged as carefully as gears.
senses.whyCN: 词语也能像齿轮那样被仔细排布。

intro.en: Device comes from Old French devis, a plan or division, which grew from Latin dividere, to divide, and it split from the verb devise.
intro.cn: device 来自古法语 devis（计划、划分），源头是拉丁语 dividere（分开），后来与动词 devise 分了家。

items.en: Dividere meant to divide or separate a whole into parts.
items.cn: dividere 指把一个整体分开、切成几部分。

items.en: Devis named a plan, a division of work or a design.
items.cn: devis 指一份计划、一种分工或一个设计。

items.en: English device first meant a plan or a heraldic design.
items.cn: 英语 device 最初指计划或纹章图案。

items.en: The sense shifted from the plan to the thing built from it.
items.cn: 词义从计划本身转到了照计划造出来的东西。

items.en: It now means any small machine, and also a trick or a method.
items.cn: 如今它指任何小型机器，也指花招或方法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vis shape, while the meaning group names useful objects and tools.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vis 这一段，近义组则给出有用的小物件与工具。

entries.definition: to invent a plan or a method
entries.definitionCN: 发明一种计划或方法

entries.definition: not direct or honest
entries.definitionCN: 不直接或不诚实的

entries.definition: an opinion about what someone should do
entries.definitionCN: 关于某人该怎么做的一种意见

entries.definition: a small useful machine
entries.definitionCN: 有用的小机器

entries.definition: a tool used for careful work
entries.definitionCN: 用于精细工作的工具

entries.definition: an object held to do a job
entries.definitionCN: 拿在手里干活的物件

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a cracked-open casing on a table and end with a writer counting repeated words.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌上一个撬开的外壳开始，落到一位反复数词的作家。

normal.en: A device begins as a devis, a plan drawn before any part exists.
normal.cn: device 起初只是一个 devis，一张还没有零件时就画好的图。

normal.en: Take one letter away and the noun becomes the verb devise.
normal.cn: 拿掉一个字母，名词就变成动词 devise。

normal.en: Anything with a switch can be called a device today.
normal.cn: 今天任何带开关的东西都能叫 device。

normal.en: Silence can be a device too, with no wires at all.
normal.cn: 沉默也能是一种手段，一根线都不用。

normal.en: A repeated phrase is a device the ear remembers.
normal.cn: 重复的句子是一种耳朵记得住的手法。

abstract.en: Picture a screwdriver beside four loose screws.
abstract.cn: 想象一把螺丝刀旁边放着四颗松开的螺丝。

abstract.en: Picture a blue light blinking on a small plastic box.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小塑料盒上闪着蓝灯。

abstract.en: Picture the same word printed five times down a page.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词在纸上竖着印了五遍。

examples.en: The device measures the moisture in the soil.
examples.cn: 这个装置测量土壤里的湿度。

examples.en: Silence was just a device to make us talk.
examples.cn: 沉默只是一种让我们开口的手段。

examples.en: The writer uses repetition as a poetic device.
examples.cn: 这位作家把重复当作一种诗歌手法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 device 记成「地歪死」：de 是分开，vis 是看，把东西分开来看，看清结构再装成一件装置。

root: 来自古法语 devis（计划、划分），源头是拉丁语 dividere（分开），与动词 devise 同源后在英语中分化。本义是计划或设计，十六世纪起转指照设计造出的物件，再引申为手段与文学手法。

sensesIntro.en: From a plan drawn on paper, to the machine built from it, to a trick or a turn of style.
sensesIntro.cn: 从画在纸上的计划，到照它造出的机器，再到一个花招或一种笔法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small machine opened on a table, its parts laid bare.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台小机器在桌上被拆开，零件都露在外面。

branches.en: The first sense is the plan turned into hardware.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是计划变成了硬件。

branches.en: The second sense is a plan that needs no parts at all.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是根本不需要零件的计划。

branches.en: The third sense is a plan made of words.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是用词语做成的计划。

branches.en: A machine and a trick both exist to get a result.
branches.cn: 机器与花招，都是为得到一个结果而存在。

branches.en: A trick and a literary device both shape how you respond.
branches.cn: 花招与文学手法，都在塑造你的反应。

intro.en: Device belongs to a family about planning, dividing and building something useful.
intro.cn: device 属于一族词，围绕计划、划分与造出有用的东西。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base dividere means to divide, and the French plan word devis grew from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 dividere 意为分开，法语里表示计划的 devis 就是从它长出来的。

more than one piece of equipment
to invent a plan or method

items.example: Devising the rules took a week.

pos.zh: 狡诈的；不诚实的；迂回的

senses.title: Cunning and dishonest
senses.definition: using secret tricks to get what you want, without being honest
senses.definitionCN: 用暗中的手段得到想要的东西，不诚实
senses.example: He is a devious negotiator.
senses.exampleCN: 他是个狡诈的谈判者。

senses.whyCN: 一个把牌藏在桌下的玩家。

senses.title: Winding and indirect

senses.whyCN: 一条离开大路又拐回来的小径。

senses.title: Using hidden tricks
senses.definition: achieved by indirect and dishonest methods
senses.definitionCN: 通过间接而不诚实的方法达成的
senses.example: They won by devious means.
senses.exampleCN: 他们靠不光明的手段赢了。
senses.why: A shortcut cut across a private garden.
senses.whyCN: 一条穿过私人花园抄出来的近路。

intro.en: Devious comes from Latin devius, off the road, de- away plus via, a way or road.
intro.cn: devious 源自拉丁语 devius（离开大路的），由 de-（离开）加 via（道路）构成。

items.en: Via meant a way or road.
items.cn: via 意为道路。

items.en: Devius meant lying off the road.
items.cn: devius 意为位于大路之外的。

items.en: Devious entered English for winding routes.
items.cn: 十四世纪 devious 以迂回路线义进入英语。

items.en: It began to describe erring behaviour.
items.cn: 十六世纪开始描述偏离正道的行为。

items.en: The cunning sense became dominant.
items.cn: 十九世纪狡诈义成为主流。

items.en: Devious now usually means sly.
items.cn: 如今 devious 通常指狡猾。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vi- road family; the near-meaning group names other words for sly behaviour.
note.cn: 形近组共享 vi-（道路）家族；近义组是其他表示「狡猾」的词。

entries.definition: To leave a course or standard; it shares via but is a verb of leaving.

entries.definition: A departure from a norm or value; it shares via as a noun.

entries.definition: Coming before; it is prae- before plus via, so on the road ahead of another.

entries.definition: Good at getting what you want by deceiving people.

entries.definition: Doing things in a secret and slightly dishonest way.
entries.definitionCN: 以秘密且略不诚实的方式行事。

entries.definition: Behaving in a way that hides the truth.
entries.definitionCN: 以掩盖真相的方式行事。

abstract.en: A track bending away from the main road and back.

abstract.en: A shortcut cut across a private garden.
abstract.cn: 一条穿过私人花园抄出来的近路。

examples.en: She saw through his devious scheme.
examples.cn: 她看穿了他狡诈的计谋。

examples.en: The devious lane doubled the walk.
examples.cn: 这条迂回的小路让步行距离翻倍。

examples.en: He was more devious than his brother.

root: 拉丁语 via（道路）→ de-＋via → devius（离开大路的）→ 英语 devious

sensesIntro.en: One road left behind: a hidden card, a bending track and a cut shortcut.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一条被离开的大路：一张藏起的牌、一条拐弯的小径与一条抄出的近路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a track bending away from the main road while a player hides a card under the table
core.cn: 核心意象：一条小径离开大路拐开，同时一个玩家把牌藏在桌下

branches.en: A player hiding a card under the table.
branches.cn: 一个把牌藏在桌下的玩家。

branches.en: A track bending away from the main road and back.
branches.cn: 一条离开大路又拐回来的小径。

branches.en: A shortcut cut across a private garden.
branches.cn: 一条穿过私人花园抄出来的近路。

branches.en: Both hide the real method.
branches.cn: 两者都掩盖真实手法。

branches.en: Both leave the direct way.
branches.cn: 两者都离开直路。

intro.en: Devious is de- plus vi- plus -ous; the road root also builds via, viaduct and deviate.
intro.cn: devious 由 de- 加 vi- 加 -ous 构成；道路这个词根也造出 via、viaduct 与 deviate。

latinIntro.en: Latin via means a road, ducere to lead and prae before.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 via 意为道路，ducere 意为引导，prae 意为在前。

definition_zh: 设计；想出；拟订
definition_en: to invent or plan something by thinking carefully
core_image: 桌上摊着草图，铅笔在纸上改了又改
scene: 几个人围着白板，把方案擦了又写，一直弄到天亮。They devised a plan to cut costs without losing staff.
sceneCN: 这里 devise 指「设计」（第 1 个义项：想出并安排出一个方案）；句意是他们设计出一个既降成本又不裁员的方案。

senses.title: Invent a plan
senses.definition: to invent a plan or method by thinking carefully
senses.definitionCN: 经过仔细思考发明出一个方案或方法
senses.example: They devised a plan to cut costs without losing staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他们设计出一个既降成本又不裁员的方案。
senses.why: A plan does not exist until someone draws its first line.
senses.whyCN: 在有人画出第一道线之前，方案并不存在。

senses.title: Think up a clever way
senses.definition: to find a clever way of doing something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 为做成一件难事找出一个巧妙的办法
senses.example: She devised a trick to open the locked door.
senses.exampleCN: 她想出一个打开锁门的巧办法。
senses.why: The obstacle stays the same; the new path is the invention.
senses.whyCN: 障碍没有变，被发明出来的是那条新路。

senses.title: Arrange a formal system
senses.definition: to create and arrange a formal system, rule or document
senses.definitionCN: 制定并安排好一套正式的制度、规则或文件
senses.example: The committee devised new rules for the contest.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会为比赛拟订了新规则。
senses.why: Rules are a machine made of sentences, and someone must build it.
senses.whyCN: 规则是用句子做成的机器，总得有人把它造出来。

intro.en: Devise comes from Old French deviser, to arrange or talk over, which grew from Latin dividere, to divide, and it shares a root with device.
intro.cn: devise 来自古法语 deviser（安排、商议），源头是拉丁语 dividere（分开），与 device 同源。

items.en: Dividere meant to divide a whole into parts.
items.cn: dividere 指把一个整体分成几部分。

items.en: Deviser meant to arrange, discuss or plan something in parts.
items.cn: deviser 指把事情分块安排、商议或计划。

items.en: English devise first meant to plan or to bequeath property.
items.cn: 英语 devise 最初指筹划，也指遗赠财产。

items.en: The planning sense grew stronger and the legal sense faded.
items.cn: 计划这一层越来越强，法律遗赠那层渐渐淡出。

items.en: It now means to invent a method, a system or a clever answer.
items.cn: 如今它指发明一种方法、一套制度或一个巧妙的答案。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vis sound, while the meaning group moves from inventing to contriving and drafting.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vis 这一段音，近义组则从发明走到设法与拟订。

entries.definition: a machine made for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为某种用途制造的机器

entries.definition: indirect or not honest
entries.definitionCN: 绕弯的或不诚实的

entries.definition: a suggestion about what to do
entries.definitionCN: 关于该怎么做的建议

entries.definition: to create something that did not exist
entries.definitionCN: 造出原本不存在的东西

entries.definition: to manage to do something by clever planning
entries.definitionCN: 靠巧妙的安排设法做到

entries.definition: to express an idea in a clear plan
entries.definitionCN: 把想法写成清晰的方案

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a whiteboard covered in crossed-out lines and end with a page of new rules.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从写满涂改线的白板开始，落到一页新规则。

normal.en: Device is the thing; devise is the act of planning it.
normal.cn: device 是那个东西，devise 是把它计划出来的动作。

normal.en: The ending decides: a hiss for the noun, a buzz for the verb.
normal.cn: 词尾定词性：名词收清音，动词收浊音。

normal.en: To devise is to divide a hard job into small steps.
normal.cn: devise 就是把一件难活切成小步。

normal.en: A locked door invites a devised trick.
normal.cn: 一扇锁着的门，正好邀请一个想出来的巧办法。

normal.en: Rules are sentences arranged until they work.
normal.cn: 规则就是被排到能用的句子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand erasing half a line on a whiteboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手擦掉白板上半条线。

abstract.en: Picture three cups on a table and a coin underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上三只杯子，其中一只下面压着硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a page of numbered rules with one blank line.
abstract.cn: 想象一页编号的规则，其中留着一行空白。

examples.en: They devised a plan to cut costs without losing staff.
examples.cn: 他们设计出一个既降成本又不裁员的方案。

examples.en: She devised a trick to open the locked door.
examples.cn: 她想出一个打开锁门的巧办法。

examples.en: The committee devised new rules for the contest.
examples.cn: 委员会为比赛拟订了新规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 devise 记成「地歪兹」：de 是分开，vis 是看，把难题拆开来看，就能设计出办法。

root: 来自古法语 deviser（安排、商议），源头是拉丁语 dividere（分开），与 device 同源。本义是把事情分块安排、筹划，后来法律上的遗赠义淡出，主要表示设计方法、想出办法与拟订制度。

sensesIntro.en: From drawing a first line of a plan, to finding a clever way past an obstacle, to writing rules that work.
sensesIntro.cn: 从画下方案的第一道线，到为障碍找一条巧路，再到写出能用的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pencil crossing out a line and drawing it again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支铅笔划掉一条线，又重新画一条。

branches.en: The first sense is the sketch becoming a plan.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是草图变成一个方案。

branches.en: The second sense is the clever turn that gets past a wall.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是绕过一堵墙的那个巧劲。

branches.en: The third sense is the plan written as rules.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是写成规则的方案。

branches.en: A plan and a trick are both shapes drawn by thought.
branches.cn: 方案与巧计，都是思考画出来的形状。

branches.en: A private sketch becomes a public system through words.
branches.cn: 私下的草图，靠文字变成公共的制度。

intro.en: Devise shares a family with device, and both grow from the idea of dividing and arranging.
intro.cn: devise 与 device 同属一族，二者都从「分开、安排」这个意思长出来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base dividere means to divide, and the French verb added the sense of planning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 dividere 意为分开，法语动词又添上计划的意思。

items.example: They devise new games each year.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年都设计新游戏。
这个测试是精心设计的。
这样的方案是设计得出来的。

items.example: The device fits in one hand.

items.exampleCN: 这些装置共用一个充电器。
这条路弯弯绕绕地往上去。

definition_zh: 致力于；献身；专用于
definition_en: to give all or most of your time and energy to something
core_image: 台灯下摊开的书，旁边放着一杯早已凉透的茶
scene: 深夜的书房只剩一盏台灯，桌上的茶早已凉透。She devoted every evening to studying old maps.
sceneCN: 这里 devote 指「致力于」（第 1 个义项：把时间和精力全给某件事）；句意是她每个晚上都用来研究古地图。

senses.title: Give time and energy
senses.definition: to give most of your time and energy to an activity
senses.definitionCN: 把大部分时间和精力投入某项活动
senses.example: She devoted every evening to studying old maps.
senses.exampleCN: 她每个晚上都用来研究古地图。
senses.why: Time is the one thing you can only spend once, so giving it is a real gift.
senses.whyCN: 时间只能花一次，所以把它给出去才是真的给。

senses.title: Give yourself fully
senses.definition: to give yourself completely to a person, cause or duty
senses.definitionCN: 把自己完全交给某个人、某项事业或某种责任
senses.example: He devoted his life to caring for the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一生献给了照顾穷人。
senses.why: A life laid down on one purpose is the oldest kind of offering.
senses.whyCN: 把一生铺在一个目标上，是最古老的一种奉献。

senses.title: Set aside for one purpose
senses.definition: to give a place, page or period completely to one subject
senses.definitionCN: 把某处空间、某页或某段时间完全留给一个主题
senses.example: The last chapter is devoted to local birds.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一章专门讲本地的鸟。
senses.why: A marked space is a promise that this subject will be met.
senses.whyCN: 划出来的一块地方，是「一定会谈这个」的承诺。

intro.en: Devote comes from Latin devovere, to vow away, built from de- and vovere, to vow, and it entered English through French.
intro.cn: devote 来自拉丁语 devovere（许愿献出），由 de- 与 vovere（发誓）构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Vovere meant to make a solemn vow.
items.cn: vovere 指郑重地立誓。

items.en: Devovere meant to vow something away, often to the gods.
items.cn: devovere 指把某物许愿献出去，常是献给神。

items.en: Devotio named the act of dedication, and also a curse.
items.cn: devotio 指奉献这一行为，也曾带诅咒之意。

items.en: English devote came to mean giving oneself to a worthy purpose.
items.cn: 英语 devote 渐渐指把自己交给一个值得的目标。

items.en: It now covers time, attention, whole lives and even single chapters.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖时间、注意力、一生，甚至单独的一章。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the devot stem, while the meaning group moves from pledging to committing and consecrating.
note.cn: 形近组共用 devot 这个词干，近义组则从许诺走到投入与奉献。

entries.definition: deep love or loyalty
entries.definitionCN: 深厚的爱或忠诚

entries.definition: loving and loyal
entries.definitionCN: 充满爱意而忠诚的

entries.definition: a keen follower of something
entries.definitionCN: 对某事物极热心的人

entries.definition: to give time or effort to a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 把时间或努力给某个目标

entries.definition: to promise to give yourself to something
entries.definitionCN: 承诺把自己投入某事

entries.definition: to make something holy by a ceremony
entries.definitionCN: 通过仪式使某物神圣

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a lamp over one open book and end with a chapter given to a single subject.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从照着一本摊开的书的台灯开始，落到专门留给一个主题的一章。

normal.en: To devote is to make a vow and then pay it in hours.
normal.cn: devote 就是先立一个誓，再用小时去还。

normal.en: The tea goes cold because the book is warmer.
normal.cn: 茶凉了，是因为那本书更热。

normal.en: A whole life can be given to one small duty.
normal.cn: 整条命也能交给一件小小的责任。

normal.en: A chapter devoted to birds is a room built for them.
normal.cn: 专门讲鸟的一章，就是为它们盖的一间房。

normal.en: Attention is the modern form of the old offering.
normal.cn: 注意力，就是古老奉献的现代样式。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp with a dark ring on the shade.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯罩上有一圈焦痕的台灯。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing a book at two in the morning.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在凌晨两点合上书。

abstract.en: Picture an empty chair pulled close to a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一把空椅子被拉近书桌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 devote 记成「地沃特」：de 是向下，vot 是发誓，低头立誓把时间交出去，就是致力于与献身。

root: 来自拉丁语 devovere，由 de-（向下、彻底）与 vovere（立誓）组成，经法语进入英语。本义是许愿献出，常指献给神明，十六世纪起转为把自己交给某个目标，再引申为把时间、空间或篇幅专门留给某事物。

sensesIntro.en: From a vow paid in hours, to a whole life handed over, to one chapter set aside for one subject.
sensesIntro.cn: 从用小时去还的誓，到交出整条命，再到为一件事留出的一章。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp burning late over a single open book.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯为一本摊开的书亮到很晚。

branches.en: The first sense is the hours handed over one by one.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是一个小时一个小时交出去。

branches.en: The second sense is the whole of a life handed over at once.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把整条命一次交出去。

branches.en: The third sense is a space marked off for one subject.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是为一个主题划出来的一块地方。

branches.en: Hours and a lifetime differ only in how many payments are made.
branches.cn: 小时与一生，只差在付了多少次。

branches.en: A given life and a given page both say: this matters most.
branches.cn: 交出的一生与交出的一页都在说：这个最重要。

intro.en: Devote has a family built on vows, loyalty and the giving of oneself.
intro.cn: devote 有一族词，建在誓言、忠诚与交出自己之上。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin vovere, to vow, and de- adds the sense of giving away completely.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 vovere（立誓），前缀 de- 添上完全交出的意思。

items.exampleCN: 他们投入很多小时练习。

items.example: He is a devotee of old films.

definition_zh: 献身；挚爱；虔诚；专注
definition_en: deep love and loyalty, or the act of giving yourself to something
core_image: 神龛前一小盏长明灯，油快尽了还亮着
scene: 小教堂里那盏灯整夜亮着，守夜的人换了一个又一个。Her devotion to the old school never faded.
sceneCN: 这里 devotion 指「挚爱」（第 2 个义项：深厚的感情与忠诚）；句意是她对那所老学校的挚爱从未消退。

senses.title: Giving yourself to a cause
senses.definition: the act of giving your time and energy completely to something
senses.definitionCN: 把自己的时间与精力完全投入某事物的行为
senses.example: His devotion to the research left little time for sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这项研究的投入让他几乎没时间睡觉。
senses.why: A cause can hold a person the way a fire holds a room.
senses.whyCN: 一项事业能占据一个人，就像火占据一间屋。

senses.title: Deep love and loyalty
senses.definition: strong love and loyalty toward a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物深厚的爱与忠诚
senses.example: Her devotion to the old school never faded.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那所老学校的挚爱从未消退。
senses.why: Love that keeps returning is love that has become a habit of the heart.
senses.whyCN: 不断回来的爱，已经成了心里的习惯。

senses.title: Religious faithfulness
senses.definition: strong religious feeling shown in prayer and practice
senses.definitionCN: 在祈祷与修行中表现出的强烈宗教情感
senses.example: The old woman's devotion was visible in her daily prayers.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老妇人的虔诚在她每日的祈祷里看得见。
senses.why: A small flame kept alive says more than a loud sermon.
senses.whyCN: 一盏被守住的小火，比一场响亮的布道说得更多。

intro.en: Devotion comes from Latin devotio, a vow or dedication, from devovere, to vow away, and it entered English through French.
intro.cn: devotion 来自拉丁语 devotio（许愿、奉献），源自动词 devovere（许愿献出），经法语进入英语。

items.en: Devotio first named a solemn vow that set a person apart.
items.cn: devotio 最初指把人分别出来的郑重誓言。

items.en: It could also mean a curse, when a person was vowed to harm.
items.cn: 当一个人被许愿交给伤害时，它也能指诅咒。

items.en: French devotion narrowed to religious dedication.
items.cn: 法语 devotion 收窄为宗教上的虔敬。

items.en: English used it for worship and for loyalty to a person.
items.cn: 英语用它表示礼拜，也表示对人的忠诚。

items.en: It now covers love, duty, study and any steady attachment.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖爱、责任、学业以及任何稳定的依恋。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the devot stem, and the meaning group names loyalty, commitment and piety.
note.cn: 形近组共用 devot 这个词干，近义组则指忠诚、投入与虔敬。

normal.en: Love becomes devotion when it comes back the next morning.
